chapter: Bass playing, avant-garde and the state of the music
title: Explaining his harmonic sense and not practicing
summary: Ware cannot explain what he does; he learned from singing in quartets and practices while working.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: But people have talked about your playing that played with you. For instance, people like Blumenthal (PHONETIC) that write, writers, but then it's difficult to talk about critics like some people say the only good critics and bad critics -- they're naturally going to reflect their point of view and what they understand about music. But then someone like Billy Howell would come along, who is not a critic, who is an educator and musician himself, and talks
about how you use simple harmonies. Well, he sees it as a harmonic sense. You talked about percussion. But how about that?

-- it's hard for me to explain because I really don't know, you know. I come up with those little quartets, singing, you know, and I can hear certain things and I try to apply them, you know? For me to even try to say actually what I did musically, it's very difficult. Because I really don't know.
But you can feel it. Like Chris says, he might hear certain thing, you might hear it another way, play it another way.

That's true, that's true. Like it's hard for me to play the same thing twice exactly alike. It's hard to do because I never studied that way. I've never really studied or practiced like you see some people get up and practice, half the day, half the night, and when I practice, I'm practicing while I'm working.
